items.title: Embassy of India — identification of mortal remains (1 Sep 2026)
items.summary: Families can check photos and descriptions of remains through Nepal police channels to help with identification. Relatives may also reach out to the listed helplines for DNA matching steps or handover information.
items.citation: Embassy of India, Kathmandu — Press Release (1 September 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Rescue teams have brought out more than 10,000 people, including over 300 foreign nationals, while about 590 foreigners from 39 countries are still missing. Teams from India, China and South Korea are helping with tunnel rescues, and relief supplies have arrived from several countries.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Nepal Police — DNA profiling for unidentified remains
items.summary: Nepal Police wants relatives of people missing in the Rasuwa and Bhote Koshi floods to give DNA samples to help identify recovered bodies. In Nepal, first-degree relatives can provide a blood sample and photos at the Nepal Police Hospital or a district police office; those abroad should send results from an authorised lab by email.
items.citation: Nepal Police HQ — Information on DNA Profiling for unidentified Dead Bodies (31 Aug)

items.source: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA)
items.title: NDRRMA — Bhotekoshi water level rising again (31 Aug)
items.summary: Water levels in the Bhotekoshi River have risen again. People in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and nearby areas should stay careful.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — public warning via official channels

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)
items.summary: After the Bhote Koshi floods, 734 bodies have been recovered and 2498 people remain unaccounted for. Over 8186 people have been rescued, though more than 400 foreign nationals are still missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River on 26 August, and teams have recovered 626 bodies while about 2400 people are still missing. Over 4450 people have been rescued so far, including more than 187 foreign nationals, with teams continuing the search in the affected districts.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal's Bhote Koshi River area on August 26, killing many people and damaging homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure. Rescue teams have recovered 538 bodies so far, while 511 people from 33 countries remain missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026

items.title: FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
items.summary: Rescue teams with helicopters have reached the mudslide site at Gyirong Port after it struck Wednesday morning. Three people have been killed and 558 remain missing.
items.citation: Xinhua (Gyirong / Tibet side) — FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods-27 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit the Bhote Koshi River area on 26 August, killing many people and damaging homes, roads, bridges and other buildings. So far 359 bodies have been recovered and 596 people from 33 countries are still missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods-27 August 2026

items.title: NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood
items.summary: Nepal's foreign ministry has opened an emergency control room to help with foreign nationals who are missing or affected by the Rasuwa flash floods. Families can call or message +977-9744441227 or +977-9744441228 between 7am and 10pm.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood

items.title: Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation
items.summary: India's external affairs ministry has set up a 24-hour control room in Delhi for the Nepal floods. Contact numbers are listed for the control room as well as the Indian embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing.
items.citation: MEA press release — Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods struck Nepal's Bhote Koshi River area this morning, damaging homes, roads and other infrastructure. So far 72 bodies have been recovered and 403 people are reported missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026

items.summary: The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu is working with Nepalese authorities on search and rescue after the floods. Families can contact them at eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com or the WhatsApp numbers +977-9851316807, +977-9709107500, and +977-9810326117.
